📰 General

David Harbour Addresses Lily Allen’s Album, Reveals Shared Writing Insights •

David Harbour has responded to details surrounding Lily Allen’s upcoming album, offering insights into his experience collaborating with the singer-songwriter. The former couple, who were together for four years before their divorce, reportedly shared a highly personal and confessional writing style. Harbour revealed that Allen’s approach involved a significant level of vulnerability and openness in her songwriting process. He described this as a key element of their creative partnership, contributing to the album’s distinctive tone.

🌍 World

Ancient Clam, Older Than Empires, Tragically Dies During Age Determination •

A 507-year-old ocean quahog clam, nicknamed Ming, was discovered in the Atlantic Ocean and was the oldest known invertebrate. Scientists attempted to accurately determine its age through a standard process involving extracting a small sample. The procedure inadvertently caused the clam’s death, highlighting the delicate nature of studying extremely old organisms. Researchers were initially focused on establishing Ming’s precise age before the fatal incident occurred.

🦅 US

UN Rights Chief Demands US Immigration Policy Overhaul Ahead of World Cup •

The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, has urged a significant reevaluation of US immigration policies. His call came in the context of the upcoming World Cup, specifically addressing concerns regarding racial profiling and surveillance practices. Türk highlighted the disproportionate impact of these policies on immigrant communities within the United States. The statement emphasizes the need for a fundamental shift in approach to immigration enforcement.

💰 Business

OPM Selects Oracle for $400 Million HR IT Modernization Initiative •

The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) has awarded a contract valued at approximately $400 million to Oracle for a comprehensive overhaul of human resources information technology across federal agencies. This initiative aims to establish a unified government-wide platform designed to streamline HR capabilities and improve data management. Oracle will be responsible for developing and implementing the new platform, focusing on enhancing agency efficiency and data security. The selection follows a competitive bidding process, marking a significant step in the government’s ongoing digital transformation efforts.

💻 Technology

Gemini App Experiences Partial Outage, Affecting Some Users Globally •

The Gemini app is currently experiencing a partial outage, with reports surfacing of users encountering “Something Went Wrong 1099 or 1076” error messages. The issue began in the early hours of Wednesday, June 10th, and has impacted users across various regions. Google has not yet released an official statement regarding the cause or expected resolution time of the disruption. Technical support teams are reportedly investigating the root cause of the problem.

🎭 Entertainment

Tyler Mane, ‘X-Men’ Star, Announces Diagnosis of Rare Breast Cancer •

Actor Tyler Mane, known for his role as Sabretooth in the “X-Men” film series, has announced his diagnosis of a rare form of breast cancer. The actor shared the news on Instagram, stating that he was diagnosed with the condition, which is typically associated with women. Mane’s Instagram post detailed his ongoing treatment and expressed gratitude for the outpouring of support he has received. Medical professionals are currently monitoring his progress as he undergoes treatment for this uncommon cancer.

🏅 Sports

Knicks Game 4 Watch Party Canceled, Alternative Celebrations Planned in NYC •

The planned outdoor watch party outside Madison Square Garden for the New York Knicks’ Game 4 against the San Antonio Spurs has been canceled due to security concerns. Organizers have shifted celebrations to Wollman Rink and Brooklyn Bowl, offering alternative viewing locations for fans. Security measures will be heightened at Madison Square Garden for the game. The Knicks are competing in Game 4 of the NBA Finals. Street closures surrounding the arena are also scheduled for the event.

🔬 Science

Giant Fossil Find Shakes Paleontology: Largest Scorpion Ever Unearthed •

Scientists have identified fossil fragments discovered in the United Kingdom as belonging to Praearcturus gigas, the largest scorpion species ever recorded. The prehistoric scorpion is estimated to have reached over three feet in length, significantly larger than previously believed giant scorpions. Initial research suggested the fossils were from a different, unidentified crustacean. The discovery challenges existing understanding of prehistoric arthropod size and evolution.

🩺 Health

Simple Daily Exercises Can Help Seniors Restore Muscle Tone and Strength •

A new article highlights five accessible exercises designed to combat age-related muscle loss in individuals over 60. The recommendations include seated exercises like arm raises and leg extensions, alongside standing movements to improve balance and mobility. Researchers suggest incorporating these daily routines can significantly boost muscle strength and overall physical function. The exercises emphasize low-impact movements suitable for those with limited mobility or joint pain. Studies indicate consistent engagement in these routines can improve daily activities and reduce the risk of falls.
